quality_checklist.overall_rationale: The paper gives a credible, detailed conceptual MBSE reference-model and V&V treatment for CubeSat development, with strong context and traceability. Empirical outcome evidence, EPS detail, named toolchain information, and reproducible model availability remain limited.

bibliographic_review_management.status_rationale: Retained as core because the full text directly addresses an MBSE-compliant CubeSat reference model and model-integrated V&V. Its EPS relevance is adjacent rather than EPS-specific.

bibliographic_review_management.title: Validation and Verification of MBSE-compliant CubeSat Reference Model
bibliographic_review_management.venue: 15th Annual Conference on Systems Engineering Research: Disciplinary Convergence: Implications for Systems Engineering Research

RQ1.rationale: The paper substantially addresses generic CubeSat mission modeling with a reusable CRM, but EPS appears only as a logical Power Subsystem block and the approach assumes intermediate domain/MBSE/SysML knowledge rather than minimal behavioral knowledge.

RQ2.rationale: It claims system-level reuse, productivity, flexibility, traceability, and reliability-requirement decomposition benefits, but not EPS-specific reliability, reproducibility, or integrability outcomes, and no outcome metrics are reported.

RQ3.rationale: The paper centers on pre-physical-development model V&V through viewpoints, requirements traces, representative missions, and mission-scenario modeling, but this is for the CubeSat system/reference model rather than EPS-specific verification.

bibliographic_review_management.lineage_overlap_notes: The paper references prior INCOSE SSWG CubeSat MBSE work on behaviors, COTS simulation, trade studies, and CRM status. This extraction treats those only as author-reported lineage within the current paper and does not rely on prior papers.

RQ1: A generic CubeSat mission can be modeled with a high-abstraction CRM covering domain, mission enterprise, space/ground segments, stakeholders, requirements, measures, use cases, and logical subsystems.
The CRM enables mission-specific tailoring by populating needs, objectives, constraints, MOEs, use cases, requirements, and physical architecture decisions.
EPS is represented only as a generic Power Subsystem logical block; no detailed EPS behavior, electrical architecture, or power budget is modeled.
The approach reduces blank-slate modeling but assumes intermediate space mission, MBSE, and SysML knowledge plus SME guidance.
RQ2: Claimed outcomes include flexibility, reuse, design/V&V facilitation, traceability, productivity, simulation-tool interfacing, and future reference-model retrieval.
Reliability appears as a non-functional requirement example that can decompose into redundancy-related lower-level requirements, but no reliability analysis or EPS reliability outcome is reported.

Reproducibility and integrability are conceptual: planned OMG specification, reusable logical elements, and COTS tool interfacing are described without model availability, metrics, or integration-test evidence.
RQ3: Verification and validation are integrated into the model via validation/verification packages, requirements traces, viewpoints, representative mission population, and V&V scenarios.
Mission-specific model viewpoints are proposed to provide objective evidence for validating and verifying the model before physical CubeSat development.
The SysML model can be configured to execute mission scenarios and interface with COTS modeling tools, but no EPS-specific or executed verification result is shown.

author_stated_limitations_gaps: Further research is needed to augment the CRM with other models for CubeSat test and evaluation.
The CRM is at least three levels of abstraction away from any physical instantiation.
Use assumes intermediate understanding of space mission analysis/design, MBSE, and SysML plus SME guidance.
Requirement relationships in Figure 4 are illustrative, not prescriptive.
The CRM activity is ongoing and expected to continue into the foreseeable future.
extractor_identified_limitations_gaps: No EPS-specific architecture, behavior, requirements, power-budget variables, or verification procedures are presented.
No named SysML tool, model version, repository, data-exchange format, or reproducible model package is provided.
No empirical metrics, baseline comparison, flight/operational data, integration-test results, or stakeholder evaluation are reported for outcomes.
No detailed lifecycle gate mapping, governance workflow, or ROI evidence is provided.
COTS simulation integration is asserted but not documented with interface details or results in this paper.
